en: Chapter on the Determination of Formless Phenomena, Section 9:
The Question on Going to Uttarakuru and Other Places.
"Venerable Nāgasena, is there anyone who, with this very body, could go to Uttarakuru, or to the Brahma-world, or to some other continent?
"There is, Great King, one who, with this body composed of the four great elements, could go to Uttarakuru, or to the Brahma-world, or to some other continent."
“How, venerable Nāgasena, could one go to Uttarakuru, or to the Brahma-world, or to another island by means of this body composed of the four great elements?
“Do you recall, Great King, ever leaping over a span or a cubit on this earth?
“Yes, venerable sir, I do recall it; ‘Venerable Nāgasena, I can leap eight cubits,’ so I say.”
“How is it, Great King, that you can leap eight cubits?
“Venerable sir, I arouse the thought: ‘I shall land here. With the arising of that thought, my body becomes light.

“In the same way, Great King, a bhikkhu possessing psychic power who has attained mastery over his mind places the body under the control of the mind and travels through the air by means of the mind.”
Thus ends the ninth chapter, the Question on Going to Uttarakuru and Other Places.
